Hi Sara — sorry for the confusion and thanks for flagging this.

We see a small but common issue where the scheduling widget's timezone dropdown can be ambiguous around region names / DST labels and occasionally fall back to a UTC offset (e.g., "UTC+1") that the browser interprets as an offset rather than a named TZ. That leads to calendar clients interpreting the ICS in the wrong zone.

Immediate plan:
- I'll send a manual calendar invite (ICS) with the TZID explicitly set to Asia/Singapore so the invite is unambiguous.
- Attaching our short demo agenda so the session context is clear.
- If you prefer, we can move the demo to a slot that works for your time zone — propose 2027-04-13 10:00 SGT or 2027-04-14 10:00 SGT. Please reply with which you prefer.

Technical note (for your IT folks): when the widget falls back to an offset label we've seen Outlook desktop treat the ICS as floating and apply the recipient's default calendar TZ which can shift the meeting. The explicit TZID avoids that.

Sending the manual invite now (separate email) and copying Marissa & Dev to create the event and confirm the Zoom link.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
